covered.evidence: server.go handleFindSub symbol && GET → findSymbols (ROUTE-FIX-002, formerly SHIM-DRIFT-085): ?query= required (missing/blank → 400 INVALID_REQUEST), present-but-blank directory/workspace → 400 (sibling handleFileList convention), declared optional selectors accepted-not-narrowing (singleton-instance convention); the truthful 200 body is the EMPTY list — the shim has no LSP integration (handleLSP reports enabled:false unconditionally), so there is no symbol producer and entries would be fabricated (the question.list ROUTE-ADD-110 precedent); undeclared methods on the sub-path keep a typed 501 (405 is not in the declared response set, session.diff ROUTE-FIX-010 convention)

server.go handleInstanceSub sub dispose && POST → instanceDispose (ROUTE-FIX-003, formerly SHIM-DRIFT-091): declared responses 200 boolean, 400 BadRequest. The shim is ONE instance rooted at the workspace directory and keeps no per-instance registry to release, so the truthful payload is the declared boolean true (the handleGlobalDispose convention, idempotent for a repeated POST). The declared 400 has one reachable client input: a present-but-blank directory/workspace query parameter answers the declared BadRequestError envelope (writeOpencodeBadRequest, kind Query — the handleSkill/handleFormatter blank query convention); valued params are well-formed and scope nothing; the operation declares no requestBody, so none is read. Non-POST keeps the pre-change 501 stub from the sub-switch default
server.go handleProject GET -> project list (ROUTE-FIX-004, formerly SHIM-DRIFT-098)

server.go handleProjectByID sub current && GET → projectCurrent (ROUTE-FIX-005, formerly SHIM-DRIFT-099): declared responses 200 Project, 400 BadRequest. The runtime keeps exactly one workspace per instance (the singleton convention of /instance and /path), so the declared Project is derived from that real workspace directory: id <- instanceID(dir) (the GET /instance singleton id), worktree <- gitWorktree(dir) (git toplevel, else the directory — the /path convention), name <- the workspace base name, vcs <- "git" only when git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree succeeds (optional enum ["git"], absent otherwise), commands <- the workspace consensus.json "commands" object when present (optional, never synthesized), time <- {created, updated} from the schema_versions ledger (earliest/latest applied_at as epoch millis, the ProjectTime unit), sandboxes <- [] (required key; the runtime spawns no sandboxes), icon omitted (optional). Served arms: a present-but-blank declared query selector (directory, workspace) answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST — the operation declares no requestBody, so the selectors are what keep the declared 400 reachable (the sessionTodo / sync.steal precedent); an unreadable schema_versions ledger answers the declared 400 (the operation declares no 5xx), never a fabricated timestamp. Non-GET on the sub-path keeps the typed 501 (405 is not in the declared set); the bare /project/{projectID} typed 404 and the git/init + directories typed 501s are untouched

server.go handleProjectByID sub git/init && POST → projectInitGit (ROUTE-FIX-006, formerly SHIM-DRIFT-100): declared responses 200 Project, 400 BadRequest. Upstream runs git init in the project worktree; the shim performs the same real effect on the instance's single real workspace (the singleton convention of /instance, /path and project.current, resolved by x-opencode-directory): when the workspace is not yet a git repo, git init runs in it via runGit (GIT_* env stripped, ctx-bounded); an already-initialized workspace is a no-op re-init (idempotent upstream). The declared 200 Project is derived by the shared deriveProject translation (same fields and sources as project.current — id, worktree, name, vcs, commands, time, sandboxes). Served arms: a present-but-blank declared query selector (directory, workspace) answers the declared BadRequestError envelope (writeOpencodeBadRequest, kind Query — the instanceDispose blank-query convention; the operation declares no requestBody, so the selectors keep the 400 arm reachable); a failed git init and an unreadable schema_versions ledger answer 400 INVALID_REQUEST (the operation declares no 5xx), never a fabricated success or timestamp. Non-POST keeps the typed 501 (405 is not in the declared set); the bare /project/{projectID} typed 404 and the directories typed 501 are untouched

server.go handleSessionByID sub message/<id> && DELETE → sessionDeleteMessage (ROUTE-FIX-035, formerly SHIM-NARROWED-005): unknown session 404, mid-turn session 409 SessionBusyError, blank/ill-shaped messageID 400 (declared pattern ^msg), a well-formed messageID the session does not hold 404 via sessionHasMessage, and a known message answers the declared boolean 200 with the truthful false — messages are memory_events rows and that ledger is append-only (SPEC-002 §2.1; triggers in migrations 017/018 abort every DELETE), so no delete engine exists and nothing was deleted

server.go handleSessionByID sub message/<id>/part/<id> && PATCH → sessionPartUpdate (ROUTE-FIX-037, formerly SHIM-NARROWED-006 in this artifact's positional ids / SHIM-NARROWED-007 in the 2026-09-29 baseline report): declared responses 200 Part 'Successfully updated part', 400 BadRequest | InvalidRequestError, 404 NotFoundError. Served arms: unknown session 404 (typed session not found), blank messageID 400, ill-shaped messageID 400 (declared pattern ^msg), unknown message 404, blank partID 400, ill-shaped partID 400 (declared pattern ^prt), a supplied body that is not a Part object 400 (p1DecodeBody), and the declared 404 for every well-formed partID. The declared 200 Part is NOT served and never fabricated: the runtime keeps no parts table (migrations/ has none) and no part-editing engine — parts are SYNTHESIZED by getMessageByID from memory_events.content as one id-less text part, so no part with a 'prt-...' id exists to update, and memory_events is append-only (SPEC-002 §2.1; triggers 017/018 abort every UPDATE/DELETE). Unlike session.deleteMessage (whose declared 200 is a plain boolean that can report the truthful false) this operation declares an OBJECT the runtime cannot produce truthfully, so the declared 404 NotFoundError IS the answer (the sessionUnshare precedent, ROUTE-FIX-015). part.update declares NO 409, so a mid-turn session is not answered SessionBusyError. NOTE: the sibling DELETE on this same path is recorded below on purpose — it is still error-contract-only (the 404 comes from the message-DELETE case, not from a part.delete route); ROUTE-FIX-036 owns giving it a dedicated handler

server.go handleSessionByID sub permissions/<id> && POST → sessionPermissionRespond (ROUTE-FIX-038, formerly SHIM-NARROWED-008 in this artifact's positional ids / SHIM-NARROWED-006 in the 2026-09-29 baseline report): declared body {response*: once|always|reject} additionalProperties false (400 malformed/missing/bad-enum, 400 ill-shaped permissionID — declared pattern ^per), unknown session 404, unknown/foreign-session/non-pending permission 404 (the resolvePermission convention: only 200/400/404 declared here, no 409), known pending permission 200 with the truthful boolean true. Field mapping mirrors the consent-store sidecar's POST /permission/{id}/resolve (ROUTE-FIX-045, commit 07f2f3c) onto the REAL approval_requests columns: reject → status 'rejected', once/always → status 'approved' with the grant scope in review_notes ('granted once' / 'granted (always)'), reviewed_at the timestamp, reviewer_id 'opencode-shim' — no decision_reason column exists. Emits the same SSE approval_resolved event the sidecar resolve handler emits (HARDEN-SHIM-01)
